hints: Focus on the oxidation number of chlorine in chlorate(V) and remember chlorine starts at 0, so it must disproportionate.
Recall that cold dilute NaOH gives NaClO where Cl is +1, while hot concentrated NaOH pushes oxidation further to +5.
Check each numbered reagent to see which one reaches +5 and contains sodium, then pick the combination that includes only that one.
walkthrough:
**Identify the target product**

Sodium chlorate(V) is $\text{NaClO}_3$. In this ion, oxygen is -2, so chlorine must be +5. We need a reaction where $\text{Cl}_2$ (0) is oxidised up to +5.

$$\text{Cl in } \text{ClO}_3^- = +5$$

**Recall the two disproportionations with NaOH**

Chlorine disproportionates differently depending on temperature and concentration. Cold dilute conditions stop at chlorate(I), hot concentrated conditions go further to chlorate(V).

$$\text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{NaOH (cold, dilute)} \rightarrow \text{NaCl} + \text{NaClO} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

$$3\text{Cl}_2 + 6\text{NaOH (hot, conc)} \rightarrow 5\text{NaCl} + \text{NaClO}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Test each statement**

Statement 1 uses hot concentrated NaOH, so it makes $\text{NaClO}_3$. This is correct.

Statement 2 uses cold dilute NaOH, so it makes $\text{NaClO}$, sodium chlorate(I), not chlorate(V). This is incorrect.

Statement 3 is just $\text{Cl}_2$ in water with no sodium present:
$$\text{Cl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{HCl} + \text{HClO}$$
It cannot make a sodium salt. This is incorrect.

Only 1 is correct, which matches option D.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean 1, 2 and 3 all give sodium chlorate(V). Statement 2 gives chlorate(I) and statement 3 gives no sodium salt at all.
options.B: Incorrect. This would mean 1 and 2 both give sodium chlorate(V). Statement 2 with cold dilute NaOH stops at $\text{NaClO}$, where Cl is +1, a classic confusion between the cold and hot conditions.
options.C: Incorrect. This would mean 2 and 3 give sodium chlorate(V). Neither does. Statement 2 gives $\text{NaOCl}$ and statement 3 gives only $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{HClO}$.
options.D: Correct. Only statement 1 is right. Hot concentrated NaOH disproportionates chlorine to chloride (-1) and chlorate(V) (+5), giving $\text{NaClO}_3$ in solution.
